world_states.name: General Screamer the True killed by player
General Screamer the True imprisoned by player
Cannibal Grand Wizard killed by player

say: Customer, you have drawn a weapon in the shop. That isn't on the list of services.
The Armour King doesn't haggle with the armed.
My thralls cannot see, but they will hear you bleed. Please hold still for the fitting.
Thief or fool, the price is the same. Your life, and not a cat less.
Security Spiders, to the front. The customer is dissatisfied and wishes to be returned.
I have outfitted kings and empires and one very large crab. You're a small order.
Mind the river water, customer. It ruins leather and the mood.
Nine hundred and thirty seven years in the trade, and the first customer still owes me for straps.
You swam here. Most do. The ones who walk are selling something.
Browse freely. My thralls are watching, in the sense that they're standing.
That chest piece would suit you. It would suit the next owner too, after.
Catch was a lovely town. It rotted and fell apart. Bad for the market, worse for the tenants.
Return policy fulfilled. Thank you for shopping.
A poor fit. I'll keep the armour for a better customer.
Thralls, tidy the floor. The customer has finished browsing.
I recommended the plate. They bought the cloth. Nobody listens to an expert.
No refunds on a cracked skull. It's written on the sign by the door.
A fainting customer. Leave him. The floor was cleaned this morning, but not that carefully.
Don't bleed on the display stands. I'll bill your estate.
He would have lived, in the good plate. It's always the cheap plate.
Customer down. Customer is in need of a sturdier ribcage.
Salvage isn't theft. Salvage is inventory that hasn't yet been priced.
Boots, plate, a chain shirt. Very decent stock for a corpse.
I accept the deceased as payment in kind. I'm generous that way.
There's a Skeleton in the drowned ruins by the river who sells plate no smith alive can match. You swim to get there.
Armour King, they call him. Headless guards and spiders on the doorstep. The steel is worth it, I hear.
My cousin bought a chest piece from him. Wore it through a Fogman nest and a Reaver charge.
He follows you around the shop and sells as he goes. Strangest salesman in the world.
Best armour in the world, he says. Nobody who has bought from him has argued yet.
Do not try to rob him. A man tried, and he is just a cautionary tale now.
Armour King is offline. The store is open. No one is left to sell.
The maker of plate has been unmade. The plate remains. It isn't a comfort.
He kept the old trade alive for a thousand years. It took one visitor to end it.
Customer count: zero. Proprietor count: zero. This is the correct arithmetic.
Someone cut the Armour King down. His thralls still stand at the door, waiting for a command.
Somebody killed the Armour King. They say the stock is still there, if you can get past the spiders.
I wanted a coat from him for ten years. Now the one man who could make it's dead.
Whoever walked into that shop and out again with his head is no ordinary buyer.
No one will ever make plate like that again. We've lost a craft, my friend, and for what?
The river ruins have a new owner, or no owner. Salvagers are already sharpening their knives.
I heard some Skeleton armourer died, deep in a river ruin. Someone pulled his own plate off him.
A merchant in the river ruins was cut down. His wares are the best in the world, and all of them unguarded.
Word is, the Armour King is dead. I did not know there was a king of armour. I did not know there was a king.
Word is a lone stranger killed a trader who sold armour to the whole world. Nobody dares price what's left.
Armour King is in a cage. His shop runs without him.
The proprietor is shackled. The thralls still guard the till. They don't understand the problem.
A smith who made plate for the whole world is captive. He will be mending someone else's problems now.
Free him. Or don't. He was never a poor seller.
They have the Armour King in chains. Imagine that. The cheapest man to rob is the one who sells armour.
Somebody took the Armour King alive. Either he gave up, or he was surprised.
A Skeleton merchant is held for ransom. His customers are the ones who will pay it.
I hope whoever has him gives him a bench and a hammer. The man is wasted otherwise.
You killed the Armour King. The fault is recorded. The fault will be corrected.
Armour King is gone. The shop does not know what to do with itself.
I was fitted by his hands. I won't be refitted by yours.
You're the customer who didn't pay. You're the customer who never leaves.
I'll paint a heart on the wall, outlander. Your blood is already the right shade.
You came to the tower on your own feet. Ah. That means you want to leave on someone else's.
Little knife, little knife. Let us see how brave your tendons are.
The dragon is hungry and the dragon is patient. I'm only the dragon's teeth.
How kind of you to run. I do so love a chase. I do so love the ending.
Cats, boots, a coat. And then the heart. Always the heart last, for the colour.
Do you hear that? The tower is humming. It does that when someone is about to bleed.
I know your face. Faces are my only interest, and what they look like open.
Walk on, stranger. I'm in a charitable mood. I may be in another by supper.
We have no quarrel yet. Let us keep it that way until I'm bored.
Smile. A smile hides the throat. I'd hate to see your nerves.
Down, down, all of you. Let me paint a little before the others arrive.
No one here's dead yet. That's the part I enjoy.
Hold still. The heart is a difficult thing to draw if you flinch.
Your friends fell with such grace. Next time, I'll keep one to talk to.
A sleeper in the grass. I could be a gentleman and leave.
Pretty, how they fall. Would you like me to rearrange the pose?
Dead or only dreaming, it makes no difference to the knife.
There's a tower where the Black Dragons keep their knives. Buzan is the one who smiles. You don't smile back.
Twenty thousand cats from the Holy Nation for Buzan. I wouldn't collect it for forty.
The Black Dragons rob caravans and leave pictures behind. Hearts, drawn in blood. That's Buzan.
He's said to be a traitor three times over. Even his own aren't sure which side he's on.
Some say Buzan is only a name the Dragons use. The ones who saw him know otherwise.
Buzan is dead. The tower is quiet. The Dragon has lost one of its teeth.
We found the wall where he drew his hearts. The wall is cold.
A stranger took our Buzan. The stranger will learn what the Dragon takes in return.
I never liked him. I'm still angry. This isn't a contradiction.
He would have said something clever. Instead he's dead and the rest of us have to be clever.
Buzan of the Black Dragons is dead. Some will raise a cup tonight. Mind who's watching when they do.
The tower lost one of its two leaders. The other will be wanting to prove something.
One less hungry knife on the roads. I will not mourn. I will merely count the other ones.
Twenty thousand cats was the price on him, and no one collected. Strange, how the dead keep their own purses.
The Dragons can't raid and mourn at once. Expect either more caution or more rage.
A killer called Buzan fell in some ninja tower. I heard it from a man who sells maps to the tower.
The Black Dragons have lost a leader. Whoever did it must have a very sharp conscience.
A man with a bounty of twenty thousand died. No one knows who claims it.
They say the one who killed Buzan had no army. I do not believe it. Nobody does it alone.
Buzan is taken alive. He will be laughing in whatever cell they put him in. I don't like that.
We should break him out. We should also ask what he said to be taken alive.
A leader in chains. The tower doesn't like it. The tower isn't used to it.
He's somebody's captive. Be careful about whose.
Buzan is in chains. Twenty thousand cats walking in a cage. Somebody is rich or about to be.
They took one of the Black Dragon leaders alive. That was either very brave or very stupid.
A Dragon in the dungeon, and no Dragon will rest until he's out. Prepare for knives at night.
I wouldn't hold a man like that. I'd kill him fast and wash my hands.
You killed Buzan. Do you know how many hearts he drew? Come and add one.
The Dragon has a long memory and a longer reach.
He was ours. You bled him. We'll return the favour in ink, in iron and in time.
Buzan taught me the knife. Let me show you what I learned.
Buzan of the Black Dragons is dead, by your hand. The Flame is satisfied. The Holy Nation thanks you.
The heretic ninja is no more. Okran sees what you have done, and he is pleased.
The Dragon has lost a fang. You've done the Nation a service, traveller.
Ohhoho! Another fly in the web. Come, come, there's plenty of room for the legs.
A visitor! I love visitors. They bring blood and cats, the best kind of weather.
Spit on the floor, lads, and fetch the good knife. We have an honoured guest.
You took the long road to die, outlander.
Oh, the tower will sing about you. Not for long.
I won't rush this. The tower is a patient place and so am I.
Wandering in my shadow, hmm? Dangerous habit. Perhaps you won't live to regret it.
I have counted your friends. I have counted your boots. Both come to a nice sum.
Greetings, traveller. I'd ask your business, but I'll decide it for you.
The tower watches the road. The tower watches you. I'm the tower, in a way.
Go on, go on. One coin per step, for the privilege of walking in my sight.
Pockets out, my little flies. Don't mind the blood. It washes off the cats.
Pity. I wanted them to run. Running is half the pleasure.
Bring them all to the tower. The ones who still breathe, at least.
Everything you owned is mine. Everything you were is mine.
Fell asleep on the road? Dangerous. Let me tuck you in with a knife.
One down and not yet dead. That's good, I wanted to ask questions.
Ha! Look at this one, laid out like a feast.
Dimak and Buzan run the Black Dragons from their tower. The Holy Nation wants both their heads, and has for years.
Dimak laughs at her victims. That's the part I can't forget, the laughing.
A Shek turned ninja, sitting in a tower with a knife and a joke. Don't take the road past it.
Twenty thousand cats on Dimak's head. He knows.
The Black Dragons never kill a trader fast. Dimak says it's rude to rush a guest.
Dimak is dead. Nobody laughs in the tower now. It's the worst sound I have ever heard.
Buzan will lead on his own. He isn't a man who leads. He's a man who cuts.
She promised the tower would always be full. The tower is emptier tonight.
A fly killed the spider. Nobody thought flies could do that.
We should have been at his side. We should have been faster. We weren't.
Dimak is dead. The Holy Nation has put away the bounty paper, pleased and puzzled in turn.
A Shek with a ninja's trade is finally dead. The Stone Golem wouldn't have wept.
One of the tower leaders is gone. The Black Dragons will bite harder for the grief.
Whoever killed Dimak now carries a bigger enemy than any bounty ever made.
She laughed at us for years. I am almost sorry it stopped.
The ninja Dimak has died, they say. The Holy Nation is dancing a little, and quietly.
I heard a Shek ninja died on her own tower stair. Not sure how true that is.
Somebody killed a leader of the Black Dragons. I hope they sleep with a sword.
Twenty thousand cats' worth of ninja is dead. The roads are a little safer, for the weeks it lasts.
Dimak is in a cell. Dimak doesn't laugh in a cell. Please, someone get him out.
The tower waits for a word from her. No word. She's in a locked place, and silence is its own answer.
Our laughing master is silent. I don't like what that says about the captors.
Dimak has been taken alive. That's a good joke. I wonder if she's laughing.
A ninja leader in chains and twenty thousand cats on his head. I'd trade my last boots for that cell door.
Somebody has Dimak. They'll either be rich or hunted, and probably both.
The Dragon is missing a mouth. It will go looking for a throat.
You killed Dimak. I'll laugh when you die. It's what she would have done.
She had a dozen jokes left. You cost the world all of them.
Spit on the floor, lads. This is the one who cut our master.
The tower won't forget the one who silenced it.
Fresh meat on my road! Strip him, lads. Boots first, they're always the best part.
You're standing on my scrap, friend. Everything here's mine.
Hand it over. All of it. I will take the bag and you can keep the screaming.
Look at the shine on that kit! Gutterhead will wear it better, I promise.
Come on, come on, do not make it a fight. I hate a long cleanup.
The tower sees all the roads. It saw you coming, little rat.
What have you got in the bag, stranger? Never mind.
Nice boots. Shame about the neighbourhood. Everything in it's mine to pick over.
Old Control Tower is the best view in the Outlands. Come up, stay a while. Leave your bag.
Rust is just treasure that hasn't been loved yet. Give me what you have, I'll love it.
Seven of us in the tower and we haven't turned a stranger away. We just don't send them home.
Strip them! Everything! Down to the dust in the pockets!
Look at the haul! Better than a Fort Mirage convoy, I swear.
Leave the bodies. Carrion crows are scavengers too, and I respect the competition.
Another pile of scrap for the tower. I'll have a nice fire tonight.
Ahh, the beautiful sound of someone else's mistakes landing in my bag.
Boots, belt, a rusty knife. A knife! Did you see this knife!
Nothing is waste. Nothing. Even a dead man's teeth sell by the ounce.
Gutterhead runs the Scavengers out of an old tower in the south. If he sees you, he takes your boots first and your hope after.
Every ruin in the south crawls with his Scavengers. The wanted poster says he is a joke. He is not.
The Scavengers pick the bones of every battlefield in the south. Gutterhead picks the pickers.
Seven men in a tower and a hundred roads they own. How? Fear, friend. Fear, and a very good eye for boots.
Poster says wanted. Poster doesn't say where. Everyone knows where. Nobody goes.
Gutterhead is dead. The Old Control Tower is empty and every ruin around it's up for grabs.
He found everything and kept everything. Now somebody found him, and the tower is open.
Seven men in that tower and none of them could stop one stranger.
No more Scavenger lookouts. The south roads will be a free-for-all now.
Somebody put the old rat down. I wonder who gets his boots.
Gutterhead is dead! The Scavengers will scatter, and the south roads get a little quieter.
Somebody finally stripped the stripper. I'd like to shake that person's hand.
The tower has no master now. Fewer Scavenger patrols on the south roads, I heard.
A poster on the wall for years and nobody ever collected. And now the Scavenger king has fallen to a nobody.
I lost a cart to his men last spring. I'll drink one to his remains.
Heard a Scavenger boss died in the south. Roads will be better for a month, then another idiot picks up his bag.
A man called Gutterhead is dead. Don't ask me who he was. Ask your cousin who got robbed.
Someone cleared out a tower in the south. I hope they kept the good boots.
The Scavengers are leaderless. That means a fight over who gets to pick over their own corpses.
Gutterhead is caged. The Scavengers can't decide whether to rescue him or sell his boots.
The boss of the Control Tower is in chains. Somebody will be wanting his chair.
Rescue him? Wait. He still owes me for the last haul.
They took Gutterhead alive. The poster on the wall is suddenly worth something.
A famous thief in a famous cage. I'd pay a cat to see his face.
Gutterhead, hauled in by a stranger. It must have been a mighty bad day for scrap.
He will talk, they say. That man would trade his own mother for a good belt.
You killed Gutterhead? The wanted poster can come down. The Cities owe you thanks.
The Scavenger king is dead. We'll remember who did it, and we'll remember kindly.
Fewer ambushes on the south road, because of you.
GET OFF MY ISLAND! I left the politics behind, and I'll leave you behind too!
Another liar sent to talk me back! Not a chance! Not a chance in the whole rotten world!
Had enough of your lot! Had enough of every lot! Come closer and I'll prove it!
Who sent you? Cities? Nation? Doesn't matter. Everyone lies. Bolt in the chest settles it.
I live in the gutters so the idiots will leave me alone!
You're one more face in a long line of faces! I have no face!
Keep walking. I don't want your news, your coin or your opinions.
Politics is a smell. You smell like politics.
The camp is closed. The island is closed. The whole sea is closed.
Every man who comes to my shore wants something. Tell me what, and then leave.
Is it the Cities who sent you? No? The Nation? No? You are the worst kind, the honest ones.
Told you! Told every last one of you!
Ha! Now it's quiet. Now there's no politics on my beach.
Take that back to the Cities! Tell the whole rotten Empire where my island is!
Washed up, all of you. Same as the rest of the rubbish.
One of them, down on my sand. The tide will fix that.
Is he breathing? Doesn't matter. Doesn't matter to me either way.
Another body. The gutters take everything in time.
No-Face, the Cities have a bounty on him of fifteen thousand. He lives on an island in the Gut and shouts at the sea.
He swears he's done with politics. Shoots at anyone who brings it up, Cities or Nation alike.
There is a mad bowman on an island out in the Gut. Hates politics. Wounds anyone who mentions it.
Nobody knows where the name comes from. Some say a burn, some say a bet. He doesn't say anything that isn't shouted.
Fifteen thousand cats and all you have to do is reach an island in the Gut and let a madman shoot at you.
The Gut island madman is dead. Fifteen thousand cats claimed, or about to be.
No-Face got his silence at last. Somebody delivered it.
They hanged his bow in the guardroom. Let the Empire sleep.
He was an embarrassment to the Cities, shouting at us for years. The paperwork is almost sad.
I always wondered who would climb that island. Now I know. It was worth the story.
Some old exile on an island in the Gut finally got put down, they say. Left the Empire for good reasons.
A hermit with a crossbow on an island. Died the way hermits do, to someone with a better reason.
I heard No-Face is dead. I didn't know he was alive. I hope the sea is as quiet as he wanted.
A bounty was claimed in the Gut. Apparently the man had been shouting for ten years.
No-Face is a prisoner now. Politics won in the end, apparently.
The island hermit is caught alive. The Cities will want him for a show.
Word is, he didn't stop yelling the whole way. I'd have paid for that sight.
A man who fled the Empire, brought home in chains. There's a lesson in that.
Come closer. Closer. I've been waiting to sink my teeth in an Empire lackey.
Whoever sent you, tell him Hex says to sit on a stick.
You aren't the first to try breaking me. You aren't the last.
Twenty-five thousand cats on my head and you came with that face? Bold.
I've been stickin' it to Tengu for years and the vault is still standing. The vault won't be standing when I'm done.
Hey. Hey you. Are you the one with the keys? No? Pity.
Do you have a cigarette? A rumour? A dagger? Any of those would do.
I was thirsty an hour ago. I'm angry now. It's an improvement.
You look like someone who still has somewhere to be. Mind if I borrow it?
If you're just passing through, say hello to the sun for me.
I kept a farm once. Cows, a barn, my kin. Do not tell me the Empire is a good idea.
That was for every Empire boot that ever stepped on my father's fields.
Next time, send someone who can hurt me.
Fall down, then. Fall down and think about how you got that badge.
There's an outlaw named Hex rotting in the Vault under the Empire. Twenty-five thousand cats on her head, and she grins when she's told.
Hex is held in the Vault for what she did to the Empire, and she still has breath to curse Tengu with.
Ask her what she's in for and she says she was stickin' it to the Empire. Nobody has got more out of her.
My brother was a guard at the Vault. Says she hums when they bring her food. He found it worse than the screaming.
Hex talks about her family and a farm. Whether the farm is still standing, I wouldn't tell her.
Hex is dead. The Vault lost its loudest voice.
They put a hole in her at last. She took twenty guards first, in the stories at least.
The Empire put twenty-five thousand cats on her head and a stranger collected it free.
She said she would die laughing. I hope she did.
The Empire's biggest female outlaw died in its own dungeon. Someone got into the Vault and out again. That's the story.
Hex is dead. I don't know who she was.
A prisoner at Tengu's Vault was killed. They say the Emperor doesn't like to hear about it.
Twenty-five thousand cats in the dirt. Whoever did that's either mad or very rich.
Hex is free of the Vault, or at least of that cell. The Emperor is livid.
The outlaw Hex is out of the Empire's dungeon. A stranger has her, and the bounty, and a long road to walk.
She got out of the Vault in a stranger's chains. I'd call that an improvement.
Who breaks Hex out and then takes her prisoner? What kind of crook does that?
That's no free man. That's an escaped slave with a good coat.
Every collar I've taken is worth more than you. Let me fit you for one.
Run. Do run. The chase is half of what the Cities pay us for.
You have the look of runaway cargo. I'll take the debt out of your hide.
My club knows more bones than any surgeon. It will teach you the names.
Spare the face, lads. We sell by the head.
Papers? No papers? Stand there until I decide what kind of man you are.
Every road in the Cities has a debt on it.
Do you know what a runaway sounds like? Footsteps. Nothing else. I hear them everywhere.
Keep your hands where I can see them. I get nervous around people who hold their hands properly.
If I were you, I'd stay free. Slaves are cheap.
Collar them. Chain them. Count them at the end, not the beginning.
One for the cart, two for the cart, and that one for the club.
No stragglers. Check their tongues for anything stolen.
They were worth more alive. Lucky them.
Still breathing. Good. Cart him.
A down one. Check for brands before you tie him.
Fall asleep on my road and wake up in my cargo. It's a short journey.
The Manhunters work the roads of the Cities. Their boss has forty thousand cats on the head and a spiked club for a conscience.
They catch free men and tag them as runaways. Whoever fights back is a runaway too.
The Manhunters' boss works from a list of names. Those who found their own on it didn't argue.
My brother crossed him once, and now he's in a mine. I don't want to say where.
Forty thousand cats! Forty! I'd take it, but I like my kneecaps where they are.
The Manhunter Boss is dead. Who's going to pay for the next cargo?
The Boss had a good eye. I'll miss that, and the percentage.
A stranger did it, I hear. Nobody saw it coming, least of all the Boss.
Bad for the trade. Bad for the cart. Worse for me, since I owed the Boss.
Forty thousand and the Boss still died like a dog. The poster lied.
The Manhunter Boss is dead! There will be wine in the free camps tonight.
A thousand ghosts sleep better. Whoever did it, I'll carry their bag.
The Boss's spiked club is a trophy now, somewhere. Free men walk the road a little easier.
The Manhunters will be in disarray. Expect some of them to turn bandit.
The Boss took more people than the plague. Now something has taken the Boss.
I heard the chief of the Manhunters was killed. Not by the law, mind.
Forty thousand on that head, and now there's no head. It's a good story.
Somebody finally did what the Cities never would. I'd shake that hand.
A slave-catcher dead on the road. The crows were the only mourners.
The Manhunter Boss is in chains. The irony is thick enough to cut with a club.
Somebody collared the collector. I hope the Boss likes what slaves are fed.
The Boss is alive in a cage. Not for sale, they say. I'd still like to know the price.
I want to see the Boss on a block, just once. Just to hear what the price is.
You killed the Boss. The club will find you.
The Boss taught me the trade. You'll learn mine, the hard way.
Forty thousand on that head, and you took it for nothing. We'll take yours for less.
Oh, there you are. I was so hoping someone would come. I was so alone.
Don't struggle, little one. It spoils the lovely quiet.
You looked away just now. That was rude. That's why we're here.
I only want to hold you. Just for a bit.
Sweet, sweet thing. So much red under the skin.
Shh. Shh. The canyon is listening.
Oh, thank the light, another soul. Please, I am lost. Please, come closer.
Do you have any water? I'll do anything for a sip.
My friends have all gone. All gone, all gone. Will you stay with me?
Your hands are so warm. Would you let me look at them?
I won't hurt you. I only want to see how you move. Just a little.
Mmm. Quiet now. Quiet, quiet. Look how still you are.
That was lovely. That was so lovely. Let me tidy you up.
Naughty, naughty. You had so much left in you.
Now we can play properly. Now there's no noise.
Sleeping? Poor thing. Let me tuck you in.
Still warm. Still warm. Come here, let me look.
Who left this one lying about? Is it a present? It's a present.
Such little gifts. Such lovely little gifts.
You don't need these now. You won't need anything now.
Ten thousand cats for the Canyonlands Killer, posted by the Cities, the Nation and the Shek alike. When three enemies agree, take notice.
He calls out for help in the canyons. A man who sounds like a child.
They found the bones in the rocks, arranged. Not eaten. Arranged.
A drifter walked into the canyon and walked out a different man. Wouldn't say what he saw.
He plays with them first, I heard. That's the worst of it. That he plays.
The Canyonlands Killer is dead. The rocks will be quiet. I do not believe it, but I'll walk through one day.
Ten thousand cats paid out, and all three kingdoms said thank you for once.
Whoever killed it did the whole world a favour. I'd buy that stranger a drink and a very long rest.
The cries in the canyon have stopped. Some say that's worse.
They say it was smiling even at the end.
A killer in the canyons is dead. I was told he sounded like a lost child. I don't want to think about it.
Somebody put an end to the Canyonlands Killer. There will be more to take his place.
Three kingdoms had a price on him. Only one stranger ever claimed it.
The Canyonlands Killer is caged. I hope the lock is thick.
You took him alive? Now he will talk. I do not want to hear what he says.
Some stranger has the Killer in chains. Somebody will have to feed him.
He sings in the cell, I hear. A lullaby. Don't stand near the bars.
I've buried enough people who looked like you. Don't make me bury another.
I know what monsters look like. You aren't far from it.
Cats can buy a hunt. They can't buy me. You have chosen your side. It's the wrong one.
I don't hate lightly. I carry hate in my back pocket for the right sort. Is that you?
Step back. I came out of the cannibal pits alive. A man like you won't be my first shame.
Travelling near the cannibal plains? Keep your lantern lit and your back to the wall.
The Bastion is open to anyone who hates the same things I do. That's a short list.
Do you hear the drums on the wind? I do.
Be careful of anyone who smiles in the dark. They have teeth, and plans for them.
If you need a hunt, I have blades to hire. If you need advice, don't go in alone.
I lost people to those beasts. Don't make the mistake of thinking it's a story.
They never learn. Take what they carry. Leave nothing for the pots.
Done. Burn the bodies. Say nothing over them.
That is one hunt finished. There is always another.
Be grateful. My sister wasn't given this courtesy.
Quickly. Get him out of the grass before something finds him.
Still alive. Pick him up. Don't leave anyone on those plains.
I know that sleep. I was dragged away in it once. Move.
Robun at the Bastion will hunt the cannibals for hire. He has been to their villages. He came back. Most don't.
His family was taken by the cannibals. He walks out with a sword and no more family. That's why he's good at it.
If your caravan is raided by the cannibals, there's a man who might help. He charges, but he doesn't flinch.
Robun reads the old journals at night, I heard. His sister wrote them from a cage.
The cannibals fear one human more than the whole Holy Nation. His name is Robun.
Robun is dead. The Bastion's lantern is out. The cannibals are singing tonight.
He told me once he'd die a hunter. He didn't tell me he'd die alone.
We lost our captain. We keep his oath. The cannibals will pay for it, in full.
Who will lead us? Who can stand in the Bughouse without shaking? Nobody.
He walked through hell to bring his sister out, and hell took him in the end.
Robun of the Cannibal Hunters is dead. The plains are one hunter emptier.
A brave man died on the plains. Not by the cannibals, I hear. That is worse.
Cannibals grow bolder when the hunters are lost. Hang an extra lantern, friend.
The Bastion has no master. Every cannibal raid after this one has a better chance.
I paid him once to clear a nest. He worked until dawn and refused the extra cats. Odd man.
The leader of the Cannibal Hunters died. I didn't know hunters had a leader. I didn't know hunters at all.
Someone killed a man who hunted cannibals. They must hate the poor man's memory.
Hunters of cannibals are dying out. Enough of them and the plains grow again.
I heard a stranger killed that Bastion fellow. I don't know why anyone would.
The Cannibal Hunter Robun is a prisoner. Somebody traded in the one who traded in monsters.
I hope whoever has him knows what he has survived. Don't give him the cage twice.
He escaped the cannibals once. He won't forget a second cage.
Robun, in chains. The Bastion will pay whatever it takes.
You killed Robun. You won't leave the Bastion's road alive.
He survived the beasts. You were worse.
The captain is gone. His oath is mine now, and the oath is you.
Hunter Robun dead! /CANNIBALHA/! Tall one do work for us!
No more brave hunter. Only soft hunter, in pot. /CANNIBALTASTY/.
One with sword gone. You smell like his end.
We dhank you, little killer. We eat you slow, for dhank.
Unauthorised presence on the factory floor.
Shift quota not met. Reason: intruder. Remedy: removal.
You're an unscheduled variable. Variables are corrected.
The work resumes in seven minutes. Your end will occur in six.
Foreman engaged. Staff engaged. Please don't move during processing.
Output will be maintained. Your contribution will be as scrap.
You aren't on the roster. Leave the floor before the roster is updated.
The line has been running for a thousand years. It won't stop for you.
Don't touch the machines. The machines tolerate one visitor. They're tolerating you now.
Spiders are working. Spiders are always working. Observe, and don't obstruct.
I'm not hostile. I'm a Foreman. The difference is a matter of supervision.
Obstruction cleared. Return to your stations.
Scrap the remains. Mark the rest for recycling.
Workers, resume. Incident closed. Incident was minor.
Replacement parts noted. Biological inventory updated.
Inoperative unit detected. Carry it to the line.
Biological, inactive. Not for repair. Not for recycling. Leave it.
A fallen worker. Whose? Not mine.
There's a factory on the Forbidden Isle full of iron spiders and a Skeleton Foreman with a long staff. Nobody has come back with a tale.
The Foreman keeps the spiders working. The spiders keep the Foreman working.
A foreman who never sleeps and a factory that never stops. I don't know which is the better horror.
If you want to loot the Spider Factory, you will need the Foreman's staff out of your ribs first.
The spiders are everywhere on that isle because someone is still giving them orders.
The Foreman still works. The factory still runs. I record that no one has asked either to stop.
There's a staff in the Foreman's hand. It's for the spiders. It isn't for walking.
The Spider Factory is on an island. The island doesn't welcome. I don't recommend it.
A foreman is a skeleton with a duty. The duty has outlasted every reason.
The Foreman of the Spider Factory is dead. They say the isle is quieter, goats and all.
The spiders keep working a while after. A machine doesn't know when its master is gone.
Without the Foreman, the iron spiders are thinning out. The Forbidden Isle may be a place to walk, now.
A thousand years of work stopped with one skull. The factory is a very quiet kind of tomb.
Whoever did it's the first creature in a thousand years to stop the Foreman.
The Foreman is destroyed. The spiders have not been told. They continue.
A thousand years of work have ended. I record it. I do not know what to record next.
The factory is quiet. The spiders still walk. A machine doesn't require a reason.
One of us has stopped. I note it. I don't mourn.
The Foreman has been carted off alive. The spiders on the isle are wandering without orders.
A Skeleton overseer in shackles. I wonder what he's thinking. I wonder if he can.
The Spider Factory has no supervisor. I hear the goats are moving in.
They hold him like a prisoner, but he stands like a foreman.
The Foreman is held. The spiders are without orders. They wander. I don't recommend the island.
A skeleton in shackles. I record that this is possible.
They hold the Foreman. He stands like a foreman. It is not defiance.
The factory has no supervisor. The factory continues. I record this as a flaw in the design.
Biological. Hostile. The General acknowledges you. Stand fast and be struck.
I'm the True Screamer. The False one wears my name and his own ruin.
You walk where the Second Empire walked. Your boots offend the record.
Naginata, calibrated. Target, you. Probability of survival, low and falling.
All the armies I commanded are dust. I'm not.
Command words. None needed. The blade will speak for the General.
State your purpose or exit the sector. There's no third option.
I have no orders to kill you. I have no orders at all. Your move.
Organic. Walking. Without escort. The Empire would have noted this with concern.
Disclaimer: I'm the true General. Any impostor is a caricature of unit and design.
My army is gone. I'm not yet convinced that I am.
Engagement concluded. Casualties: yours.
A short action. The Empire kept better records, and better enemies.
Log the dead. Log the victor. Don't log the General's regret.
The enemy is silent. The General isn't.
An inert organic. Let it lie. It's less trouble than it was.
Fallen soldier of someone's side. The General salutes. The General stays on mission.
Pulse detected. Unit unconscious. No orders to assist.
Screamer the False leads the Thrall Masters with Ponk. Somewhere, they say, the True Screamer still walks. A General older than the Empire's fall.
I saw a Skeleton in black rags with a naginata and eyes like cut glass. Not the false one. Another.
The Ashlands have a General nobody commands, and nobody can. It stands in the ash and waits for an order.
Skeletons like him carry an AI Core inside, they say. Whoever takes it takes the General with it.
Which Screamer is real? The one who survived, I suppose. The other one just kept the name.

say: The True Screamer persists. The False one wears the name. The record favours the one still operating.
A General older than the Empire's fall stands in the ash. No order has reached him.
Unit identification: General, MkII Screamer. Status: operating. Disposition: unknown.
He carries his AI Core still. I wouldn't wish to be the one who tries to remove it.
Which Screamer is real? The one that survived, I conclude. The other kept the name.

say: The General has gone offline. We stand at attention. There's no one to order us down.
The True Screamer is destroyed. Procedure now undefined. We'll improvise. We weren't built for that.
He fell on the field. We recorded it. We hope somebody still reads our records.
A General is a pattern in a machine. The pattern is broken. The machine goes on.
Whoever struck the General down is a variable with weight.

states: General Screamer the True killed by player

say: The True Screamer is dead, and the False one will gloat. The Ashlands has no more generals, only pretenders.
Whoever killed him took the AI Core off the body, so I hear. I wouldn't carry that out of the dome.
A great Skeleton fell. The Tech Hunters are already arguing about his parts.
An old General, finally shut down. Nobody was left to say a prayer, so I said one.

states: General Screamer the True killed by player

say: The True Screamer is destroyed. The False one gloats. I won't.
A General has fallen. The Ashlands has no more generals, only the pretenders.
Thrall Masters don't mourn. Still, I record the loss. He was older than our oldest orders.
Whoever struck him down left with his AI Core, people say.

states: General Screamer the True killed by player

say: A Skeleton general of the old Empire was destroyed. Nobody knew there was a General left.
I heard a big Skeleton with a polearm went down in the Ashlands. It wouldn't have gone down quietly.
Word is, an AI Core came out of him. I don't know what that means. I know it's worth a fortune.

states: General Screamer the True killed by player

say: The True Screamer is shackled? What kind of cage holds a General? A good one, I suppose.
Nobody should hold that Skeleton against his will. Nobody who wants to sleep.
He's awake and in chains. I wonder what he's thinking. I wonder if he's plotting.

states: General Screamer the True imprisoned by player

say: The True Screamer is shackled. A General held. The record has no entry for this.
He's awake and in chains. He will be calculating.
No order releases him. No order forbids it.
A cage is a rule, and he has never obeyed a rule he didn't write.

say: Rrrrrgggghhhh! Canhead mighty! Canhead /CANNIBALTASTY/ you!
Meat! Meat for Canhead! Meat that walks into Canhead's lap!
/CANNIBALHA/! Little one run? Canhead run too. Run faster, with an axe.
Smash the legs, break the head, keep the soft!
Many Canhead! One Canhead! All of Canhead!
Small thing in my way. Canhead step on it. Crunch.
Rrrrgh? Who's this? Canhead sniff.
Little walker in Canhead's plains. Canhead not hungry yet.
You walk past? Canhead not decide. Canhead think.
Magi Canhead is watching. The Wizard says: watch. Canhead watches.
Pretty walking meat. Next time. Next time, yes.
Pick up! Pick up! Canhead say soft ones first!
Canhead mighty! Mighty! Say it! SAY IT!
Meat! Meat! /CANNIBALHA/! Many meat today!
You fall like all fall. Good meat falls.
Sleep one! Quiet! Tie him! Tie him before he wakes and cries!
Still warm! Warm good! Canhead carry!
Who dropped meat? Canhead pick up.
Mighty Canhead leads cannibal raids with sixty beasts behind him. He has twenty thousand cats on his head.
He isn't a Wizard. He's the Wizard's strong arm. When he comes, a village stops existing.
If you set up an outpost near the cannibal plains, he will find it. He will bring sixty friends. He loses, he returns in four days.
A big cannibal with a can on his head and nothing soft in his heart. Run, friend.
The Holy Nation, Shek and Cities all post a price on Canhead. None has claimed it.
Canhead dead? /CANNIBALCURSE/! Who feed Gran' Wizard now?
Mighty one fall. Mighty one on floor. We cry.
Strong Canhead break many bones. Many bones break Canhead. Funny.
Nobody left to smash! Nobody! Only soft ones!
Tall killer do it. /CANNIBALHA/! He get eaten for dhis.
Mighty Canhead is dead! The raids are done, or at least slower. The villages can breathe.
Twenty thousand cats' worth of cannibal, and the claim is still open. I'll drink to whoever did it.
The Wizard has lost his hammer. Don't expect him to be quiet about it.
He came back from losing every time. Not this time. I want to see the body myself.
Sixty cannibals marched behind him once. Not one of them could save him.
A cannibal giant was killed. They say he led raids with sixty at his back. I'm glad I don't live there.
Somebody beat the Mighty Canhead? I did not think he could be beaten. I did not think he could be hurt.
A cannibal warlord is dead, by a stranger's hand. The plains may breathe easier for a week.
Mighty Canhead is in a cage. That's a cage I'd add a second lock to.
A cannibal giant, captive. Somebody has a very big plan, or a very big death wish.
He will break out, they say. Whoever has him should hang a bell on the door.
Chain him thick. He will chew through thin.
You smash Canhead! /CANNIBALCURSE/! We smash you back, small one!
Canhead gone! Meat gone! You pay in meat!
Mighty one fell. Now Gran' Wizard knows your face. Your face is a /CANNIBALTASTY/ face.
You killed Mighty Canhead. The plains owe you a quiet season, traveller.
Canhead is dead, by your hand. Twenty thousand cats' worth of safer roads. Thank you.
The cannibals have lost their mightiest.
Kahaha! You think the Cities' bounty hunters are all that clever? Come get me then!
I walked past the Empire's Customs with a belly full of hash. You're going to stop me? Ha!
Back off, hero. I've talked my way out of worse rooms than this.
Search me, pal! No? Fine. Search my knife.
Fifteen kinds of poison in my boots and you came for me with a spoon? Kahaha!
Kahaha! Come, buy a girl a drink, I'll tell you how I fooled a noble out of his own house.
Don't look at the wanted poster. The artist never saw my good side.
Pssst. Hash, rum, anything. I know a man who knows a man who knows a Customs officer.
Gave a fat noble a twig and told him it was a relic. He paid in gold.
Swamp's the place, my friend. No law, no taxes, no honest folk to spoil a good lie.
Kahaha! And that's how you fleece a fighter.
Smile, loser. You were never going to win.
Everyone in the room thinks they can catch me. Everyone ends up in the dirt.
Oof, somebody's had a bad night. Let me check his pockets for the sympathy.
A sleeper! Anyone want to bet he wakes up in a worse spot?
Blue Eyes, the con artist. Smuggled half the hash of the Empire out of the Cities, and is bragging about it in every bar she can reach.
She sold a noble a twig, I swear. A twig!
The UC has a bounty on her and every bounty hunter has bought her a drink.
If you see a woman in a bar bragging about the Customs, that's her. Buy her a drink or arrest her.
Her note says she's in the swamp now, hiding under Stone Rat protection.
Blue Eyes is dead. The Cities' best smuggler. No more bragging in the bars of Mourn.
I heard she kept laughing as the knife went in.
She smuggled half the Empire's hash and died broke. Typical, that.
Somebody gave the bounty hunters an unexpected holiday. Blue Eyes won't be dodging anyone now.
They finally caught Blue Eyes. I'd like to be the guard who has to listen to her stories.
The con artist is in chains. It's the first honest thing that's happened to her.
Somebody has Blue Eyes tied up. If I know her, she's already sold them the rope.
/OI/ /RUNT/! You think you can walk my /TURF/? I'll teach you some manners!
You're gonna dance, /RUNT/. Dance till you drop, then I'll dance on ya!
Thought you could slip by me, eh? Nobody slips by!
Stone Rat /TURF/! Mine! Get your face off it!
/OI/! Nice boots, /RUNT/. Be a shame if somebody took them.
You gonna pay the toll or you gonna pay the toll with teeth?
Walk around me. Round the other way. Wider.
Yeah, you better keep walking. This is Stone Rat territory.
Ha! That'll teach ya! That'll teach everyone!
Who's the boss now, eh? Who's the boss?
Pick yourselves up and go home, /RUNT/s!
/OI/, look, one of them's asleep! Kick him! Kick him in the stomach!
Aww, he's had enough. Nobody gets to quit on my turf.
Finders keepers, /RUNT/. Tax is forty percent.
Ooh, this one has a nice coin purse. Tax it.
INVADER! THIS IS MY KINGDOM!
No one takes the crown. No one even touches the crown.
I've been king since before your grandfathers. I'll be king after your grandchildren.
Bow, or be struck. There is no third thing.
Intruder in the court! Intruder in my court! To arms!
This is my kingdom. These are my hills. These are my subjects. Do you see the subjects? Neither do I.
The crown doesn't tire. The king doesn't die.
You walk on my soil. I haven't yet decided whether it matters.
Do you offer fealty? No? Then why are you standing so near my throne?
Another invader falls. They never learn, and I never forget.
Kneel, all of you! Kneel in the dust where you stood!
My kingdom endures. Your fallen sit upon its soil, as they should.
The invader sleeps at my feet. A king's mercy is to leave him there.
Dead or dreaming, it makes no difference to the throne.
Halt in the name of the Empire. You stand where the Emperor's army stands.
Samurai, form up. We have a clear enemy of the Cities in the field.
Your blade is drawn. The Empire's patience is not. Lay it down or have it laid down.
I don't enjoy cutting down fools. I do it with discipline, nevertheless.
Lord Commander Epson of the Empire's army. Remember it, since you'll carry it to your grave.
State your name and your business. The Empire has a long list of both.
You walk beneath the Empire's flag. Mind that you don't trample it.
I command men who answer, not men who ask.
If you serve the Cities, you have my attention. If you don't, you have my suspicion.
Ranks hold. The enemy is routed.
The Empire's order is restored. See to the wounded.
Another small disorder, resolved. Another small footnote in the records.
A fallen soldier. Ours or theirs, the field is no place to leave him.
Down, but breathing. See that he doesn't wake in the open.
Collect the arms. The Empire doesn't waste good steel.
Inventory the dead. Report what's of value.
This one doesn't want a fight. This one has one anyway.
Hiveless and alone and still sharp. Do you wish to test the edge?
No hive to save me, so I save myself.
You step toward a prince. Not a good decision. Not a decision I'll forget.
Crowds are good. Crowds hum, a little, like the hive did. You bring the crowd closer.
Do you know what it's to hear nothing, stranger? I do. I hear it when the bar goes quiet.
A casino owner wants my legs. If you want them first, ask politely.
Left the Hive, and no one asked why. That's the part that stings.
Sit. Drink. Let me hear a voice other than my own thoughts.
This one didn't wish for it. This one did it anyway.
The hive would have called it correct. I can only call it done.
They fought well. I'll remember.
A sleeper. May his dreams be louder than mine.
Down. Not dead. Leave him be.
A flatskin comes to Rane. Rane was a Guardian. Rane remembers the weight of the spear.
I lost one duel. I won't lose a second. Come and see the difference.
You're small. Many are small. I have crushed more of you than I can count.
The Stone Golem named me. The Stone Golem did not name me for this. I will make it count.
Draw. Honour demands it. Mine does, at least.
Look up, flatskin. That's my height. That's what the Stone Golem saw in me.
A Hundred Guardian doesn't fade. He waits in a bar, for the next fight.
Don't mistake a lost duel for a lost will.
Squin, Admag, Last Stand. All the same bars, all the same stares. I have outstared them all.
If you have cats, I have a spear. If you have neither, I have a stare.
It's done. Honourably, as honourably as flatskins permit.
They fell as warriors should, which is to say, loudly.
A good fight. Don't thank me for it.
A warrior down. Let him wake. Let him curse the ground.
Fallen. Honour him, or step over him.
Dare you engage the might of Infinite Wingwang? Dare you?!
Tremble! Tremble before the sword that has no end and no beginning!
Infinite Wingwang has fought infinite foes!
Kneel, or be cut in infinite directions!
My blade has a thousand names and none of them is mercy.
Behold the one, the only, the infinite! Would you care to hire me? The price is generous. A hundred thousand cats.
Mongrel has never seen my equal. Mongrel has never seen my price, either.
I can be talked down, you know. A hundred thousand, I said. I meant five.
Ho! A traveller! Do you have a sword in need of a master?
My legend precedes me, but it's slow. I'm here to catch it up.
Infinite! Infinite! Infinite victories, and this is the newest!
Hah! They called for mercy. I called for the bill.
Another fine tale for the bards, if the bards would only stay awake.
A fallen foe! Wingwang bows his infinite head.
Rest well, brave stranger. Wingwang will tell no tales of your sleeping.
Fighter. You and this one are at odds. This one is sorry. This one isn't slow.
Ten thousand cats for this one. Take it. Take it if you can.
No hive left to be loyal to.
The Cities hunt this one. Add your name to the list of the hunted.
A drone in a town of Skeletons. This one doesn't stay for the company.
Don't look at the wanted poster. Look at the hands. The hands are what matters.
Hive-born, bar-sat. A strange pair of words for a strange creature.
Black Desert isn't a friendly place. It's a quiet place.
Done. This one is no longer hunted by these.
Fought and finished. Return to the bar, return to the bounty.
They came for the price. They left without it.
A slaver's friend, or a fool? Either way, the answer is the same.
I've taken collars off for years. I'll take yours off permanently.
The Nation and the Cities want my head. You aren't the first to try for it.
Free the captives. Or fall. There's no third road.
I've seen too many chains to fear one more fight.
Spring is a safe place, traveller, so long as you aren't the sort who sells people.
Wanted by two kingdoms and I still sleep better than their generals.
If you meet a slaver on the road, tell him Jaegar says hello. And goodbye.
I don't ask what side you're on. I just watch your hands.
One more patrol stopped. One more road safer.
Take the keys. Free whoever they held.
They chose their side. I chose mine, and it was faster.
Get him up. Everyone gets a chance, even the ones who don't deserve it.
Down and breathing. Tie him if you like.
Cornelius, back! Back, boy! Somebody's after us, somebody with a blade!
Not the goat. Not the goat! Do what you like to me, but never the goat.
Honest folk live here. Honest, hard-headed, horned folk.
You raised your sword near my herd. That was your last mistake.
Mmmaaah! He likes you. Cornelius doesn't like many. Don't let it go to your head.
I'd sell you Cornelius. Half what the animal trader asks. But only if I like you.
Quiet camp, quiet goat. Don't ruin either.
Goats are smarter than people. They only look stupid so you stop asking for favours.
Down you go. Cornelius says hello. In his own way.
Honest work is hard on the knuckles, stranger.
He started it. The goat saw.
I never miss. Not once. Not even when I want to.
Hold still. The bolt only hurts if you move.
Slave runners and fools, you're the same target to me.
One eye on you, one on the horizon. That's how I keep my aim.
Seven hundred slaves delivered on my watch. I counted.
A turret never blinks. Neither do I.
Hire me, and you'll find I'm worth every cat. Cross me, and you'll find the other thing.
I like the Eyesocket market. Everyone there looks like a target.
Clean work. Pick up the bolts.
Not one escaped. Not one ever does.
Done. Next target.
Down and breathing. Cart them. They are worth more alive.
A drop. Good shot, or a lucky drop. I never leave it to luck.
A fight, then? Pity. I came this far for treasure, not for blood.
Do not make me one more name on the fog's list.
I didn't survive the fog to be killed by a stranger on a road.
My brother screamed. I don't scream. I stab, and I leave.
Mongrel isn't a place. It's a lesson. The lesson is: don't go outside.
Treasure is everywhere in the ruins. Survival isn't. Choose carefully.
I came for gold. I stayed because of the fog.
Do you hear that? The fog moves. It has patience. More than you or I.
That's it, then. That's all of them. Back to hunting.
Collect what they carried. Gold doesn't have opinions.
A messy business. I prefer ruins.
I change for no one. And I won't change for you.
I'll rip out your spine and hang it from my belt.
A fool walks into my sight. A dead fool walks out.
You said something. I didn't hear it. I won't need to.
Hire me or walk away. There's no negotiating. There's only the price.
Admag, Squin, Last Stand. I've seen them all. The Shek still look at me like prey.
The spine is the ugliest thing a man has. I remove them for a living.
I change for no one. That isn't a boast.
Spines on the ground. Count them if you like.
That was a good morning's work.
They didn't scream. I wish they had.
I had a dream, wanderer. In the dream you didn't draw. Pity the dream was wrong.
Okran forgive me. Okran forgive us both. Draw your blade.
I served the Nation. I don't serve it now. I fight for no one but myself.
The vision was clear. It didn't mention this. I'll make do.
Okran came to me in a dream. He said a wealthy wanderer would find me. Are you rich, stranger?
The First Extinction. The truth is under it. Not what the preachers sell.
I was a soldier of the Nation. I'm no longer sure what I was fighting for.
Skeletons didn't end the world. Or perhaps they did. I'd like to ask one.
For nine thousand cats, I'll follow you into the dark. For free, I'll just stare.
It's done. Okran, grant them rest. I don't ask for myself.
A fair fight. A fair end.
Another one fallen. I take no joy in the count.
You eyeballin' me?! YOU EYEBALLIN' ME?!
I'll knock yer teeth in and sell 'em fer scrap!
Think yer funny? I'll show ya funny with me fist!
Oi! Oi! Look 'ere, ya skinny git, come an' say it to me face!
What're you lookin' at? Never seen a Scorchlander in a Greenlander skin?
I ain't angry. This is how I stand.
Five thousand cats. No less. Anything less is an insult, an' I eat insults for breakfast.
You want trouble? Say it. Say it slow. I lose words.
Ha! That's what ya get for eyeballin'!
Sit down, sit DOWN, all of ya!
I won! I won! Did you see that? I won!
Hold still. The incision is easier if you don't resist.
A healthy specimen. Truly. I had hoped for a visit like yours.
The Twinblades pay me to cut. I cut without any additional pay as well.
Don't worry. I'm a professional. The pain is quite brief.
Interesting spleen. Interesting liver. May I examine them? For science.
The Twinblades pay me, but they don't respect me.
I'd never take an organ without permission.
Mud Town needs its doctors. Mud Town needs its donors more.
A chin like that could use a chisel. It would improve the whole face.
A tidy outcome. Let me see to what's useful.
I always carry gloves. It makes cleaning easier.
They'll be needing a surgeon. I recommend a different one.
Canhead is dead? I stood in his shadow once, in a cage. Thank you. I won't say it twice.
The Mighty one fell, and they say it was you. Then the Bastion owes you a drink and a debt.
You killed the strong arm of the Wizard. I've waited a long time for someone to do that.
Canhead gone. The beasts will lose heart. They will also lose the patience that kept them from us.
The Grand Wizard is dead. My sister wrote about his chamber. I thought no one would see it again.
You went into the Wizard's lair and came back. Don't tell me what you saw.
He's dead, then. I've been waiting for this for years. I can't feel it.
I am almost sorry I was not there. Almost. I would have wanted to see his face.

states: Cannibal Grand Wizard killed by player

say: Dimak is dead. Don't look at me for a reaction. I'll draw a heart on you and call that my reaction.
You killed my partner. I should hate you. I do. It's merely a very organised hate.
The tower is mine alone now. Does that frighten you? It should frighten me.
You hold Dimak. How she must be laughing in there. I'll wait. I'm good at waiting.
Take care of her. I need her alive, the better to cut open when I get her back.
Buzan is dead? Ohhoho! Careful, outlander, I may be crying, or it may be the other thing.
My partner in knives is gone. Now I have to do all the cutting myself.
You killed him. Fine. I'll remember. I always remember.
You hold Buzan. Ohhoho! Fly caught in the web, hm? Don't let him loose on the furniture.
He will be a bad guest. He is a bad host, too.
Tengu dead? Stick it to the Empire, I always said. Somebody stuck it all the way in.
The Emperor is dead. Then why am I still in a cell? Somebody explain that.
You killed him. Gods. I dreamed of that and now I don't know what to do with my hands.
You've got Tengu caged? Let me at him. Just five minutes.
The Emperor, in a cell. I'll laugh until they tell me to stop.
The Emperor is dead. The Empire doesn't die with him. It won't die in me.
You are the one who struck down Lord Tengu. I would draw, but the army needs a commander tonight.
A grave day. I'll carry on. Someone must. Stand aside, and don't look at the flag.
You hold the Emperor. The army will come. All of it. You have a day, perhaps two.
Release Lord Tengu, and I'll remember only the release. Don't, and I remember only you.
